edition_notes: Pandasaurus Games / Catch Up Games, ©2024; designers Romaric Galonnier & Anthony Perone; art Noëmie Chevalier; 2-5 players, 20 min, ages 8+

items.rule: Place the game mat in the center of the table.

Shuffle all Courtier cards and, without revealing them, randomly remove cards according to player count: 2 players remove 30 (60 left), 3 players remove 18 (72 left), 4 players remove 6 (84 left), 5 players remove none (all 90 used).
Deal 3 face-down Courtier cards to each player; players look at their own cards secretly.
Place the remaining Courtier cards face down as a draw deck near the mat.
Deal each player 2 Secret Mission cards, one blue and one white; players keep them secret and may look at them anytime but never reveal them until game end.
Unused Secret Mission cards go back in the box without being looked at.
Randomly choose the first player.
Play proceeds in clockwise turns, starting with the first player.
On your turn you must play all 3 cards in your hand, face up (except spies), placing exactly one card in each of 3 areas: the Queen's table, your own domain, and an opponent's domain.
You may play the 3 cards in any order, as long as there is one card per area.
At the Queen's table, place the card in the column of its family, choosing to place it above or below the mat.
After playing your 3 cards, draw 3 new cards from the top of the deck for your next turn.
If the deck was empty when you needed to draw, that was your last turn; wait for the round to finish.
Assassin (2 per family): when played in an area, you may eliminate one other Courtier card in that area; the card is removed from the game. Use is optional.
An assassin played at the Queen's table may eliminate any card there, regardless of family or above/below placement, even a spy (without looking at or revealing it).
Guard (3 per family): cannot be eliminated by assassins; once played it cannot be removed.
Noble (4 per family): at game end counts as two cards, in a player's domain or at the Queen's table.
Spy (2 per family): always played face down; no one may look at it, not even the player who played it.
A spy played at the Queen's table is placed in the Queen's column, above or below her seat on the mat, hiding its family.
The game ends when the Courtier deck is empty and no one has cards left in hand.
At game end, reveal all spies; those at the Queen's table move to their family's column keeping their level (above stays above, below stays below).
A family with more cards above the mat than below is esteemed; more below than above is fallen from grace; equal is neutral (nobles count as two cards).

Each courtier in your domain or in front of you (including those placed by opponents) in an esteemed family gives you 1 point; each in a fallen family loses you 1 point; neutral families have no effect; nobles count double.
Each player reveals Secret Missions; each fulfilled mission card is worth 3 extra points, unfulfilled ones are worth nothing.
The player with the most points wins.
In case of a tie, tied players share the victory.
